Q: PostCSS error "tailwindcss requires PostCSS 8" when npm start A:

From Tailwind CSS v4 onwards

Starting from v4, the TailwindCSS package has separated the PostCSS and CLI modules - which are not needed by everyone - into dedicated packages: @tailwindcss/postcss and @tailwindcss/cli.

For installation, @tailwindcss/postcss is required from v4 onwards, which in tested with PostCSS v8.4.

Conclusion: From v4 onwards, using PostCSS 8.x is a minimum requirement.

  • Get started TailwindCSS with PostCSS - TailwindCSS v4 Docs
npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss

Deprecated Create React App

Deprecated

Create React App was one of the key tools for getting a React project up-and-running in 2017-2021, it is now in long-term stasis and we recommend that you migrate to one of React frameworks documented on Start a New React Project.

If you are following a tutorial to learn React, there is still value in continuing your tutorial, but we do not recommend starting production apps based on Create React App.

Source: facebook/create-react-app

Q: Do I learn React before JavaScript? I'm confused A:

I totally understand your confusion. Every frontend beginner feels this at the start, so you’re on the right track already.
First, focus on learning JavaScript basics (variables, functions, loops, DOM). Use videos from Hitesh Choudhary or Apna College, and read from MDN Web Docs.

Practice small projects like a to-do app or counter, that’s where real learning happens.

Don’t jump into React yet. It feels hard because JavaScript is not strong. First get comfortable with JS, then React will become much easier.

Q: How to get started with building a simple LLM-based models using Python? A:

You’re asking the right question, but let’s ground it: you don’t “start by building LLMs.” You start by using them well, then gradually understand how they work.

Right now, your leverage is not in training models—it’s in learning how to shape behavior through prompts, structure, and data flow.

The minimum concepts you actually need are simpler than most people think: understand what a transformer roughly does (tokens in → probabilities out), what tokens and context windows are, and why LLMs are fundamentally next-token predictors, not reasoning engines. Once that clicks, prompting stops feeling like magic and starts feeling like controlled input design.

Don’t get stuck in theory first. If you go deep into transformer math too early, you’ll burn time without building intuition. Start with APIs, build small systems, and let the gaps in your understanding pull you into theory naturally. That’s a much faster path.

A practical path looks like this: take Python, connect to an LLM API, and build something small but real—a structured extractor (turn messy text into JSON), a validation layer (like what you were already exploring), or a simple Q&A system over your own data. You’ll quickly run into prompt design, temperature tuning, and response formatting. That friction is where real learning happens.

For resources, skip random “AI hype” videos and look for content that shows end-to-end builds, not just explanations. Focus on things like prompt engineering patterns, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and basic embeddings. Those are immediately useful and give you a systems-level view of how LLMs are actually deployed.

If you want a clean roadmap in one line:
API → prompt control → structured outputs → embeddings/RAG → only then peek into transformer internals.

If you stay consistent with that flow, you’ll move from “I tried the API” to “I can design LLM-powered systems” much faster than most beginners.

Q: Bochs VESA/VBE Missing DDC Compatiblity A:

See https://github.com/bochs-emu/VGABIOS/blob/master/vgabios/vbe.c#L2733 . You need to set CX=0 not just for BL=1 reading of data, but also for BL=0 checking for extension. Brown's interrupt list does not mention CX register in that call but I bet actual normative VESA VBE/DDC standard does (that standard is mentioned in VBE Core standard, but I couldn't find its text). VGABIOS says CX = Controller unit number which sounds logical.

EDIT: Indeed it is in the standard, and there's more! (VBEDDC11.PDF):

3.2.1 00 - Report VBE/DDC Capabilities
Input:
AH= 4fh VESA Extension
AL= 15h VBE/DDC Services
BL = 00h Report DDC Capabilities
CX = 00h Controller unit number (00 = primary controller) (*)
ES:DI Null pointer, must be 0:0 in version 1.0 Reserved for future use

(*) This refers to the monitor port number. When version 1.0 of the document was developed it
was assumed that one graphics controller had only one monitor port. Later controller designs
have multiple monitor ports per graphics controller. This parameter selects the monitor port
number from which the function reads an EDID block

So this should get you through the verification.

and when I cut out the verification, my entire program just hangs

What do you mean by that? It hangs in the BIOS code reading EDID? Because if not then the only thing happening in your program after that is the hang-loop.

If it does hangs in BIOS reading EDID then it looks like Bochs bug. VGABIOS does the faithful thing of actually reading EDID from DDC just like real hardware BIOS would, and Bochs emulates the DDC to provide EDID you gave it. So if it hangs in that exchange then it would seem like Bochs bugs out in that emulation. If that's the case, the best case of action is to go straight to Bochs team and file a bug.
